newsitem.title: USA: Russian debt prices down sharply on IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Russian debt prices down sharply on IMF news.

text.p: Russian debt prices were sharply lower on news that the International Monetary Fund failed to reach a conclusion on whether to give Russia the latest tranche of a $10 billion three-year loan, sources said.
"More than anything, there is a little bit of nervousness and some people are taking a little bit of money off the table," said one emerging markets debt trader.

At 1425 EDT/1825 GMT, Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans were off 2-1/8 at 74-3/8 bid and mark loans were down two percentage points at 78 bid. Russia's when and if IAN bonds were off 1-1/2 at 65-3/4.
The Russian Central Bank said in a statement released in Moscow earlier today that the IMF was worried about Russia's ability to meet its commitments on revenues and other issues.
The IMF declined to comment on the Russian statement.
Although the IMF news weighed on Russian debt prices, some sources believed it was just an excuse for some market participants to take profits.

"I think people have used it (the IMF news) as an excuse to take some profits because the Russian bonds are way up (on the year)," said Peter Allen, head of emerging markets research at Bank of Boston.
Market sources said Russia would still be able to issue a $500 million dollar Eurobond, but noted that the deal might be pushed back a couple of weeks because of market conditions.
"The Eurobond is still coming," said Allen. But he noted that it is possible the deal could be delayed a few weeks.
"I think it will be delayed a bit because of market conditions but it will get done," said another source.
The issue, which has been talked about in the Euromarkets for months and was expected to begin its roadshow in mid-November, is expected to carry a maturity of up to five years, sources added.
